item.title: myAiVideos: An open-source pipeline for automated Chinese short-video production
item.description:
myAiVideos: An open-source pipeline for automated Chinese short-video production

myAiVideos is a new open-source engineering project designed for the automated production of Chinese-language short videos. It covers the full pipeline from topic discovery through creative generation, visuals, audio, and post-production, all the way to distribution.

🔍 Overview

The system is built as a modular platform that coordinates multiple AI models to handle generation and quality gating. Its architecture is designed to be decoupled, allowing individual layers of the pipeline to be independently replaced.

🧩 How it works

The project utilizes a seven-layer pipeline architecture:

  • L1: Topic
  • L2: Creative
  • L3: Visual
  • L4: Audio
  • L5: Post-production
  • L6: Distribution
  • L7: Optimization

Orchestration is managed by a FastAPI core, while a Java gateway acts as the platform governance layer. The gateway handles authentication, routing, circuit breaking, metering, and observability. Key technical mechanisms include:

  • Multi-model failover: The Java gateway aggregates DeepSeek, Qwen, and GLM using Resilience4j protection to automatically rotate failed providers.
  • Prompt anchoring: Maintains the visual identity of subjects across video segments.
  • CLIP gating: Rejects off-prompt keyframes early using text-image consistency checks.
  • Audio-video sync rescue: Employs a four-tier strategy involving audio tempo adjustments, video padding, and narration rewrites.

⚙️ Key details

The system provides full-stack observability by propagating trace_id across Java and Python environments and offering Langfuse call-tree visibility. Metering and rate limiting are handled via an AOP aspect that captures token and cost data without requiring code changes, aggregated by tenant. The production-ready setup includes SSE progress streaming, single-segment regeneration, and rolling log archives.

Component Technology / Model
Gateway Spring Boot 3.5, WebClient, Resilience4j, Caffeine, Prometheus
Text LLM DeepSeek
Multimodal Moderation Zhipu GLM-4V
Visuals Kling v2.5
Speech Synthesis Volcengine / MiniMax TTS
Transcription faster-whisper

🚀 Availability

myAiVideos is available as an open-source engineering project. It supports local execution using Docker Desktop version 24 or higher. Node.js 20 or higher is required for frontend development, while Python 3.11 or higher is needed for local execution without Docker or for running host tests. Health endpoints are available for the Python API, Java Gateway, and Frontend.

#OpenSource #VideoGeneration #FastAPI #Java #AIModels

Source: myccarl/ai-shortVideo-pipeline

item.title: Agent-based trading simulation using Google ADK and A2A protocol
item.description:
Agent-based trading simulation using Google ADK and A2A protocol

This project demonstrates an agent-based trading system simulation featuring distinct agents for trading logic and risk management, communicating via the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol. It includes a web-based simulator UI to configure, run, and visualize trading strategy performance.

🔍 Overview

The system consists of three main services interacting via HTTP and the A2A protocol. It leverages the open A2A protocol for standardized, interoperable communication between the agents. This allows agents built with different frameworks to discover capabilities and interact securely. The entire system is built using the Google Agent Development Kit (ADK).

🧩 How it works

The workflow begins with the Simulator UI taking simulation parameters from the user. It then runs the market simulation loop. For each step, the Simulator calls the AlphaBot service via A2A tasks/send, providing current market data and portfolio state. AlphaBot analyzes the data to determine a potential trade signal. If a trade is proposed, AlphaBot calls the RiskGuard service with the trade proposal and portfolio state. RiskGuard evaluates the proposal against configured rules and returns an approval or rejection. The final trade decision is returned to the Simulator, which updates the portfolio state based on executed trades.

⚙️ Key details

  • AlphaBot: Implements a Simple Moving Average (SMA) crossover strategy to propose trades. It calculates SMAs to determine BUY or SELL signals and updates its internal state.
  • RiskGuard: Evaluates trade proposals against configurable risk rules, including max position size and max portfolio concentration.
  • Simulator UI: A FastAPI-based web application that allows users to configure parameters for market conditions (initial price, volatility, trend), trading strategy (SMA periods, trade quantity), and risk rules. It visualizes results using Plotly, displaying price action, SMA indicators, portfolio value, and trade execution markers on interactive charts.
  • Deployment: Includes scripts for easy local execution and deployment to Google Cloud Run. Dockerfiles are provided for building container images for each service, facilitated by Google Cloud Build.

💡 Why it matters

The project demonstrates how distinct AI agents can collaborate in a specific domain (trading) using the A2A protocol. By separating trading logic from risk management into different agents that communicate securely and interoperably, the system showcases a modular approach to building multi-agent applications where each agent focuses on a specialized task.

#AIAgents #GoogleADK #A2AProtocol #TradingSimulation #FastAPI

Source: kweinmeister/agentic-trading

item.title: Idun Agent Platform Is No Longer Maintained as Open-Source Project
item.description:
Idun Agent Platform Is No Longer Maintained as Open-Source Project

The Idun Agent Platform is no longer maintained. Its code stays open source under the GPLv3 license, and its official documentation remains online for reference.

🔍 Overview

Idun Agent Platform was created as an open-source, self-hosted production wrapper for LangGraph and Google ADK agents. It allows developers to deploy agents as production-ready FastAPI services without vendor lock-in.

Teams building AI agents typically face a tradeoff: building a custom production wrapper (combining FastAPI, traces, guardrails, and an admin UI), which is slow, or adopting SaaS solutions like LangGraph Cloud or LangSmith, which introduces sovereignty trade-offs. Idun provided a third path by offering a self-sufficient FastAPI process installed via a single pip install command on local or private infrastructure.

⚙️ Key details

The platform is distributed as a single wheel bundling three Python packages:

Package Description
idun_agent_engine The engine SDK providing the FastAPI app factory, Model Context Protocol (MCP) registry, observability, and guardrails.
idun_agent_standalone Provides the idun CLI, admin REST API, and UIs for chat, administration, and traces.
idun_agent_schema Contains the Pydantic configuration schemas.

Built-in platform capabilities and features include:

  • AG-UI copilotkit API and bundled chat UI
  • Admin panel and managed prompts
  • 15+ guardrails
  • MCP tool governance
  • OpenTelemetry observability and dedicated trace store
  • OIDC and SSO integration
  • Memory persistence and messaging integrations

🛠️ Usage details

  • Prerequisites: Python 3.12 or 3.13.
  • Installation: pip install idun-agent-engine.
  • CLI: The idun executable provides commands including setup, serve, init, hash-password, and agent serve via idun_agent_standalone.
  • Workflow: Users create a directory (such as my-agent/), save the required files, and run the engine from within that directory or via an absolute path.
  • Path Resolution: The graph_definition: "./agent.py:graph" setting is resolved relative to the directory where idun init is run.
  • Endpoints: Launching the service opens a chat UI at http://localhost:8000. Settings, MCP servers, guardrails, and SSO are configured at /admin, while trace data is available at /admin/traces.

🚀 Availability

  • Maintenance Status: No longer maintained.
  • Licensing: Code remains available open source under GPLv3.
  • Documentation: Stays online for developer reference.

#LangGraph #FastAPI #OpenSource #AIAgents #Python

Source: Idun-Group/idun-agent-platform

item.title: Python Agent Full-Stack Demo for E-Commerce After-Sales Scenarios
item.description:
Python Agent Full-Stack Demo for E-Commerce After-Sales Scenarios

A new full-stack Python Agent demonstration for e-commerce after-sales scenarios has been released, migrating a Dify prototype into a code implementation.

🔍 Overview

  • The project is a personal learning and technical demonstration utilizing fictional data and fixed demo identities, rather than a production customer service system.
  • It covers FastAPI, SQLite, LangChain, LangGraph, Chroma RAG, Langfuse, pytest, Docker Compose, and Vue 3.
  • Current test status includes 157 passed pytest tests locally, successful Vue production builds, and an accepted synthetic policy request on Langfuse Cloud v4.86.0.

🧩 How it works

  • Verifiable policy QA features include policy source citations, evidence display, safe fallback without evidence, and constraint rules for refund time limits, quality issues, logistics, and privacy boundaries.
  • Tracked model links record requests, LangGraph nodes, and model generations using the Langfuse Python SDK and LangChain CallbackHandler.
  • Security and authentication features map tokens to subjects, while the server reads roles and customer bindings from the SQLite tenant membership table instead of trusting caller-supplied values.

⚙️ Key details

Component Technology / Detail
Backend & Architecture FastAPI, SQLite (data/support_agent.db), LangChain, LangGraph, Chroma RAG
Frontend & UI Vue 3, Vite, Dashboard, Intelligent Customer Service, Orders, Approvals, Knowledge Base, Evaluation, and Observability pages
Observability & Testing Langfuse, pytest, Docker Compose, GitHub Actions
Constraints Read-only order queries; approval records approved_demo without executing real refunds, address changes, or deletions

🚀 Availability

  • Source code and learning materials are available, including five chapters of code walkthroughs, a fault case library, a requirements traceability matrix, and run verification records.
  • Run locally using Docker Compose to automatically start mock services and connect the agent, with Vite forwarding /api requests to the local FastAPI backend.

item.title: New Dockerized React/FastAPI app replicates LLM Council for model comparison
item.description:
New Dockerized React/FastAPI app replicates LLM Council for model comparison

A new React/FastAPI application is available for comparing model answers, peer rankings, and a chairman’s synthesis, inspired by Andrej Karpathy’s LLM Council concept.

🧩 How it works

The application allows each conversation to select OpenRouter or Ollama, its specific models, system prompts, and an execution mode. It supports persistent conversations, attachments, and streaming with cancellation and partial-result recovery. Execution is handled through bounded and idempotent model runs, with runtime settings controlled by administrators.

⚙️ Key details

  • Dependencies: The project uses a committed uv.lock and frontend/package-lock.json to ensure reproducible dependencies.
  • TOON statistics: Token representation comparisons are provided, but these are explicitly not provider billing.
  • Ports: The backend is published loopback-only at http://127.0.0.1:8001, while the frontend is published on port 80.
  • Proxy Limits: The frontend nginx.conf and optional nginx/nginx.conf files both set client_max_body_size to 25m. A 20 MiB image becomes approximately 26.7 MiB in base64, which can successfully upload but receive a 413 error at the proxy. To support the full API image limit, the setting must be increased to 40m and the proxy layer rebuilt.
  • Resources: The backend container has a 1 GiB total memory limit in Compose. PDF workers on Linux can each have a 1 GiB virtual-memory ceiling, with two workers per API process.
  • Databases: Compose does not provision PostgreSQL or MySQL servers. Adding PostgreSQL requires exporting base runtime dependencies with --extra database and rebuilding the image. Finance and embeddings extras similarly require explicit image packaging.
  • Environments: Python 3.10+ is declared by the project, with CI and the backend image using 3.12. Node 20.19+ or 22.12+ is required by the locked Vite release; the frontend image uses Node 22, while CI tests Node 20.
  • Configuration: In Docker, keeping a specific build-time setting empty utilizes the same-origin nginx proxy. Changing this setting for built assets requires a rebuild.

🚀 Availability

Running the application requires a running Docker engine and current Docker Compose v2. The default backend Dockerfile exports base runtime dependencies only.

#OpenRouter #Ollama #Docker #FastAPI #LLMCouncil

Source: DmitryBMsk/llm-council-plus

item.title: OneRAG Launches Production-Ready RAG Framework with Multi-Provider Flexibility
item.description:
OneRAG Launches Production-Ready RAG Framework with Multi-Provider Flexibility

OneRAG is a production-ready Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework built with Python and FastAPI that supports seamless switching between multiple vector databases and language models through simple configuration changes. The framework offers 1-line config swaps for 6 vector databases (Weaviate, Pinecone, Qdrant, ChromaDB, pgvector, MongoDB), 5 LLM providers (Gemini, OpenAI, Claude, Ollama, OpenRouter), and includes an OpenAI-compatible API for easy integration with existing codebases. With over 2100 tests and support for hybrid search (Dense + BM25), it enables developers to start locally without API keys using Ollama LLMs, scale to production without rebuilding, and maintain compatibility with OpenAI SDK code via the /v1/chat/completions endpoint. Setup is straightforward: clone the repository, sync dependencies, copy the quickstart environment file, and launch the service. Sample data is preloaded and ready to use, while the framework automatically generates environment files if missing.

#RAG #AI #FastAPI #LLM #VectorDB #OpenAI

Source: notadev-iamaura/OneRAG

item.title: Programming Navigation Launches Open-Source AI Quiz WeChat Mini-Program
item.description:
Programming Navigation Launches Open-Source AI Quiz WeChat Mini-Program

Programming Navigation has launched a new open-source educational project: an AI quiz WeChat mini-program built on Taro, React, FastAPI, and DeepSeek. Developed by Programmer Yupi and the Programming Navigation team using Vibe Coding and OpenSpec methodologies, the project is designed to teach the full workflow of AI programming, from requirement analysis to deployment and release within the WeChat ecosystem.

🧩 Core Functionality

The mini-program supports three primary methods for generating quiz questions, allowing users to customize learning paths without relying on fixed question banks:

  • One-sentence topics: Users input a brief concept or description, and the AI generates a corresponding set of questions.
  • Private document RAG: Users can upload PDF, Word, Markdown, or plain text files. The backend parses, chunks, and vectorizes the text into a Chroma vector database to generate questions strictly based on the uploaded private knowledge.
  • Web search integration: For time-sensitive or cutting-edge topics, the system utilizes web search to ensure generated questions reflect the latest facts.

The interface supports single-choice, multiple-choice, and true/false questions. Upon submission, the system immediately highlights correct and incorrect options and provides concise explanations and knowledge point categorizations. After completing a set of questions, the system generates a personalized AI review report that includes a mastery score, a list of weak knowledge points, a three-sentence summary, and learning suggestions, along with experience points rewards.

⚙️ Technical Architecture

The project employs a front-end and back-end separated design:

  • Front-end: Built with Taro 4 and React 18, including TypeScript and Sass.
  • Back-end: Powered by Python 3.11+ and FastAPI, utilizing Pydantic v2 and Uvicorn.
  • AI Orchestration: Uses LangChain and LangGraph to manage large language models and retrieval logic. Specifically, a ReAct autonomous decision agent is built on LangGraph to determine search keywords and execution rounds for web queries.
  • Data & Storage: Uses MySQL with aiomysql for asynchronous connection pooling and Tencent Cloud COS for object storage.
  • AI Services: Integrates DeepSeek for question generation and reporting, Alibaba Cloud Bailian for embedding and text-to-image generation, and Tavily for web search.
  • Authentication: Implements silent login via WeChat jscode2session and JWT, while also supporting an optional login architecture that allows unregistered visitors to experience the core quiz process.
  • Deployment: The back-end is containerized with Docker and deployed to WeChat Cloud Hosting, completing necessary AI service category applications, ICP filings, and domain configurations.

💡 Educational Context

This repository serves as a hands-on teaching project for the Programming Navigation AI Quiz Learning Mini-Program course. The curriculum covers 6 major business modules and over 30 functional points, aiming to allow students to complete the full development cycle and gain resume-ready skills in less than a week. The course includes video tutorials, written notes, resume writing references, interview questions, and one-on-one Q&A services.

#AIProgramming #WeChatMini-Program #RAG #LangGraph #FastAPI #EducationalProject

Source: liyupi/yu-ai-learn

item.title: Generative AI Project Template with FastAPI, NiceGUI, and Ollama
item.description:
Generative AI Project Template with FastAPI, NiceGUI, and Ollama

A new generative‑AI project template combines FastAPI, NiceGUI and Ollama for rapid prototyping.

🔍 Overview

  • FastAPI backend and NiceGUI frontend for chat.
  • Local Ollama or cloud models through LiteLLM.
  • uv workspace tooling, tests, Docker Compose and GitHub releases.
  • Requires Make, Bash, Git and uv.

🧩 How it Works

  • Clone the repo: git clone https://github.com/AmineDjeghri/generative-ai-project-template.git.
  • Navigate into it: cd generative-ai-project-template.
  • Install dev tools: make install-dev.
  • Copy the example env: cp .env.example .env.
  • Configure INFERENCE_* and EMBEDDINGS_* in .env for your model provider.
  • Start the app: make run.
  • Open the frontend at http://localhost:8080 or the backend API docs at http://localhost:8000/docs.
  • For local Ollama: make install-ollama then make run-with-ollama.

⚙️ Key Details

  • make docker-compose – Backend, frontend and Ollama in containers; Compose 2.24+.
  • make docker-compose-cuda – Same stack with GPU access for Ollama; NVIDIA drivers required.
  • make docker-compose-rebuild – Rebuild containers after source changes.
  • make run-backend / make run-frontend – Start either application separately.
  • Python PyTorch extras are optional for model development; Ollama inference runs outside Python.
  • make install-dev installs Git hooks in a checkout; make pre-commit-install reinstalls them.
  • make test-local runs offline tests.
  • Before a PR, configure the integration services and run make check – includes live LLM/Ollama/API tests.
  • make help lists all targets.
  • make deploy-doc-local previews documentation.
  • uv provisions the Python version set by requires‑python in pyproject.toml.

🚀 Availability

  • Repository: https://github.com/AmineDjeghri/generative-ai-project-template.
  • Local frontend: http://localhost:8080.
  • Backend API docs: http://localhost:8000/docs.

#FastAPI #NiceGUI #Ollama #Docker #Python

Source: AmineDjeghri/generative-ai-project-template

item.title: Flexible GraphRAG v0.11.0 Release Introduces New Desktop App and State Options
item.description:
Flexible GraphRAG v0.11.0 Release Introduces New Desktop App and State Options

The v0.11.0 release introduces an early version of a Desktop App built with Tauri and Rust alongside various backend and architectural updates.

🚀 Availability

  • New v0.11.0 release on 11/16/26.
  • Includes an early version of a Desktop App (Tauri/Rust) around the React, Vue, or Angular UI with 5 Flexible GraphRAG tabs.
  • Adds browsing, ingesting, searching, and graph viewing (5th tab) of local files and folders with auto-sync support.

⚙️ Key details

  • The backend is written in Python, utilizing LlamaIndex and LangChain as peer frameworks.
  • LlamaIndex serves as the default for each pipeline stage, while LangChain can be selected per stage via environment configuration.
  • The API is built as a REST FastAPI service.
  • Frontend options include Angular, React, and Vue TypeScript frontends, alongside an included MCP server.
  • An optional lighter Docker-free configuration uses SQLite as the auto-sync incremental update state store (INCREMENTAL_STATE_STORE=sqlite) along with embedded stores such as LanceDB, BM25, and LadybugDB.
  • Databases and dashboards can be enabled using the provided Docker Compose layout.

🧩 Capabilities and Integrations

  • Supports 14 data sources (10 with incremental auto-sync).
  • Supports 15 property graph databases, 4 RDF triple stores, 10 vector databases, OpenSearch, Elasticsearch, BM25 search, Alfresco, and Nuxeo.
  • File and folder browser available via Browse… in the Alfresco, Nuxeo, CMIS, SharePoint, OneDrive, Box, S3, Azure Blob, GCS, and Google Drive data source forms for both desktop and web UIs.
  • Optional ingest pipeline, hybrid search, and AI query can run through customizable Langflow visual flows utilizing 12 custom Langflow components.
  • Optional ingest can run on a CocoIndex (Rust engine) pipeline reusing the same sources, targets, parsers, and KG extractors, adding step-level memoization and automatic delete reconciliation.
  • Optional integration with Hyland OpenArch as a search and vector store, as well as a store for data sources and document state.

item.title: OpenHands Cloud Introduces Scheduled and Event-Driven Automation Execution Service
item.description:
OpenHands Cloud Introduces Scheduled and Event-Driven Automation Execution Service

A new automation execution service has been developed for OpenHands Cloud, providing support for both scheduled and event-driven automation workflows.

🔍 Overview

The Automation Service allows users to manage and execute agent workflows based on predefined schedules or external triggers. Key features include:

  • Scheduled Automations: Run OpenHands conversations on a cron schedule.
  • Event-Driven Automations: Trigger automations via webhooks, such as GitHub events.
  • API Key Management: Per-user API keys for secure automation access.
  • Run History: Track automation runs with status and results.

🧩 How it works

System responsibilities are divided across several components:

  • Automation Service: Owns automation definitions, cron scheduling, webhooks, run history, dispatch, and sandbox lifecycle orchestration.
  • Agent Server and OpenHands/software-agent-sdk: Execute agent conversations and own agent/tool behavior, workspaces, events, and API endpoints.
  • OpenHands/typescript-client: Provides typed browser access to the Agent Server API.
  • OpenHands/OpenHands: Owns the Agent Canvas UI and frontend integration.

The codebase is structured into specific modules:

File Description
app.py FastAPI application entry point
router.py API routes for CRUD operations
scheduler.py Background scheduler for cron jobs
dispatcher.py Dispatches pending runs to OpenHands
models.py SQLAlchemy models
schemas.py Pydantic schemas for API

⚙️ Key details

The service is built using Python 3.12+ and uses uv for dependency management. For storage, it utilizes PostgreSQL, with testcontainers available for testing.

Database migration and creation rules include:

  • SQLite databases are migrated on startup.
  • PostgreSQL databases are not migrated on startup unless AUTOMATION_RUN_MIGRATIONS_ON_STARTUP=true (or 1) is set. When set, each replica runs alembic upgrade head before serving requests, using an advisory lock so concurrent replicas take turns. A failed migration stops the replica from starting.
  • Setting AUTOMATION_CREATE_DATABASE_IF_MISSING=true (or 1) instructs migrations to connect to the postgres database and create the target database if missing. This requires the database user to have the CREATEDB privilege.

🚀 Deployment

For local development, dependencies can be installed using uv sync --group dev, and the application can be run with uv run uvicorn openhands.automation.app:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --reload.

Container deployment can be built and run using Docker:

  • docker build -t automation -f containers/Dockerfile .
  • docker run -p 8000:8000 automation

The service is deployed via the deploy repository at https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/deploy. Docker images are automatically built and pushed to ghcr.io/openhands/automation on every push to main and on tags.

#OpenHands #Automation #Python #FastAPI #DevOps

Source: OpenHands/automation

item.title: LangGraph‑FastAPI‑Streamlit Toolkit Enables Deployable AI Agent Services
item.description:
LangGraph‑FastAPI‑Streamlit Toolkit Enables Deployable AI Agent Services

A new open‑source toolkit delivers a complete stack for running AI agents. It combines a LangGraph agent, a FastAPI service, a Python client, and a Streamlit chat interface, all wired together with Pydantic schemas.

🔍 Overview

  • The repository provides a LangGraph agent built on version 1.0 features such as interrupt(), Command, Store, and langgraph-supervisor.
  • A FastAPI service exposes the agent via streaming and non‑streaming endpoints and also via the AG‑UI protocol for front‑ends like CopilotKit.
  • A client library lets external code call the service.
  • A Streamlit app offers a user‑friendly chat UI with voice input/output, a “Previous Chats” sidebar, and a star‑based feedback component linked to LangSmith.

🧩 How it Works

  • Data models and runtime settings are defined with Pydantic in src/schema/.
  • The service runs asynchronously (async/await) to handle concurrent requests efficiently.
  • Advanced streaming supports both token‑based and message‑based streams.
  • Multiple agents can be hosted simultaneously and addressed by URL path (see /info for available agents and models).
  • A basic RAG agent uses ChromaDB for retrieval‑augmented generation.
  • Content moderation is enforced through the Safeguard module, which requires a Groq API key.
  • Chat history for each user‑agent pair is accessible via /threads and shown in the Streamlit sidebar.

⚙️ Key Features

  • Human‑in‑the‑loop support (interrupt()).
  • Flow control with Command objects.
  • Long‑term memory via Store.
  • langgraph-supervisor for supervising agent execution.
  • Streaming and non‑streaming FastAPI endpoints.
  • AG‑UI protocol compatibility.
  • Voice interaction in the Streamlit UI.
  • Star‑rating feedback integrated with LangSmith.
  • Robust unit and integration tests.
  • Dockerfiles and a Docker‑Compose setup for rapid development and hot‑reloading.

🚀 Availability

  • Install the package with uv (recommended) or pip install ..
  • At least one LLM API key is required to run agents.
  • The Docker configuration is the simplest way to set up the environment and see immediate code changes reflected in the running services.
  • Source structure includes:
    • src/agents/ – agent implementations
    • src/schema/ – protocol schemas
    • src/core/ – LLM definitions and settings
    • src/service/service.py – FastAPI service
    • src/client/client.py – client library
    • src/streamlit_app.py – Streamlit UI
    • tests/ – test suite

💡 Practical Impact

  • Developers can prototype, test, and deploy AI agents without building infrastructure from scratch.
  • The asynchronous design and Docker support streamline scaling and local iteration.
  • Integrated moderation and feedback mechanisms help maintain safe and user‑centric interactions.
  • Compatibility with AG‑UI opens the door to a variety of front‑end experiences.

#LangGraph #FastAPI #Streamlit #AIagents

Source: JoshuaC215/agent-service-toolkit

item.title: Development of a RAG-enabled Chatbot using LangChain and LLaMA
item.description:
Development of a RAG-enabled Chatbot using LangChain and LLaMA

A new RAG-powered chatbot implementation has been developed using LangChain to orchestrate an LLaMA model and NVIDIA embeddings. The system is designed to provide context-aware responses by retrieving relevant documentation from a FAISS-backed vector store.

🧩 How it works

The system processes information by generating embeddings for documents, storing them in a FAISS index, and retrieving context for the LLaMA model during query generation. The pipeline supports both basic and RAG-enabled reasoning, with performance verified through LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation techniques.

⚙️ Key details

Component Function
LangChain Orchestrates LLM components and pipeline chaining
LLaMa Handles text generation based on retrieved context
FAISS Enables efficient similarity search and document retrieval
NVIDIA Embeddings Generates vector representations of documents
FastAPI Exposes the pipeline via RESTful APIs
Gradio Provides an interactive frontend for user testing

📂 Project Structure

  • server_app.py: FastAPI server implementation
  • 08_evaluation.ipynb: RAG pipeline implementation
  • docstore_index/: FAISS document store directory
  • frontend/: Gradio interface code
  • requirements.txt: Project dependencies

#RAG #LangChain #LLaMA #FastAPI #FAISS

Source: misterseyiayeni/retrieval-augmented-generation
